=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Preliminary point: the "FINAL / agreed at principal level" framing

The preamble asserts that the positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are "not intended to be re-opened". Treat this as a negotiating tactic, not a fact. Our baseline instructions (100%, AUD 24m, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law) say nothing about caps, baskets, time limits or knowledge qualifications having been agreed. Please confirm with the Wattlebridge principals whether anything beyond the headline terms was actually conceded. Unless and until that is confirmed in writing from our side, every "FINAL" item below is open. The "market context" paragraph is also self-serving: it quotes the seller-friendly end of the range on every metric simultaneously, and the Disclosure Letter itself (para 11) concedes that "no expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included".

Note also that the general disclosure covers "DD-002 to DD-012". Ask what DD-001 is and why it is omitted.

---

## A. Liability regime (Clauses 8.3, 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5)

**1. General cap – 20% (AUD 4.8m).** Low for a deal where the key risks are already identified and quantified (Bluefen ~AUD 3.6m revenue p.a., Riverlark AUD 3.2m, Ironquay IP, privacy incident). Push for 30–50% on general warranties, or accept a lower general cap only if (a) the specific indemnities below sit outside it and (b) we price in W&I insurance. More important than the number is what sits *outside* it (see items 3–5).

**2. De minimis / basket.** AUD 25k per claim and AUD 250k deductible (excess-only) basket. Push for: de minimis AUD 10k; a *tipping* basket (recover from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded); and express aggregation of claims arising from the same or related facts (the three Sandbar renewals at AUD 110k each are a live example of a series that should be treated as one matter).

**3. Fundamental / title / capacity warranties subject to the same caps and time limits – reject outright.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Title and capacity warranties should be capped at 100% of the price and run for the full statutory limitation period (6 years in NSW; 12 if the SPA is a deed, which we should insist on). This is the single most serious structural departure in the draft.

**4. Time limits.** 18 months for general warranties is too short to catch one full post-completion audit cycle and renewal cycle; push for 24 months. Tax warranties/indemnity: at least 7 years (aligned to ATO amendment periods plus a buffer). Fundamentals: statutory period. The proposal that "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" inverts the normal position – it means any carve-out we miss defaults to the seller. Reverse it: limitations apply only where expressly stated, and never to fraud, wilful concealment, fundamental warranties, the tax indemnity, specific indemnities, completion obligations or leakage/debt-free adjustments.

**5. Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature".** Must be carved back. Non-exhaustive carve-outs: fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation; wilful default; the specific indemnities; the price adjustment / debt-free mechanics; completion deliverables (including the Riverlark release); and any statutory rights that cannot be excluded (notably misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law – a non-reliance clause can affect reliance in evidence but cannot contract the right out, and we should not sign anything that purports to).

**6. Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge, including matters "discoverable from the data room or public records" – reject in its entirety.** This is a constructive-knowledge exclusion that, combined with the general data-room disclosure in Schedule 7, would eliminate essentially every warranty claim: anything in the data room is "disclosed", anything not in it but on a public register is "discoverable". If we must concede anything, the fallback is actual knowledge of a short list of named Wattlebridge individuals of the specific facts giving rise to the claim *and* their appreciation that it constituted a breach – and even that fallback should be resisted where the warranties are the price-allocation mechanism for known risks.

**7. Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter para 1 – general disclosure of the whole data room and public registers – reject.** Require "fair disclosure": specific disclosure, in sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter disclosed, against the specific warranty it qualifies. Public-register disclosure should be limited to listed searches (ASIC, PPSR, court lists, IP Australia) at a stated date, with copies attached. The Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026; today is 5 November. We need a bring-down disclosure at signing and again at completion, and the warranties repeated at completion.

**8. Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" – reject.** Tax: standard tax indemnity (pre-completion tax, uncapped or capped at price, 7-year survival), plus pre-completion tax return conduct provisions. IP: this is a SaaS business – IP title is the asset we are buying. IP ownership warranties should sit with the fundamentals (100% cap, long survival), particularly given the Ironquay issue.

---

## B. Specific deal issues

**9. Bluefen (DD-002) – ~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of revenue; change-of-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3.** The Seller Update says the consent "is addressed"; the Disclosure Letter says no final written consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Those statements are inconsistent and the Disclosure Letter is the accurate one. Position:
- Unconditional written Bluefen consent, in a form approved by the Buyer, *and* evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived by Bluefen, as a condition precedent – not "treated as satisfied on delivery" of a letter we haven't reviewed.
- "Reasonable endeavours" is the weakest standard; require "all reasonable endeavours" with specific steps (approach within X days, Buyer involvement in discussions, no commitments given to Bluefen without Buyer approval).
- If the consent is not obtained by the long-stop date, Buyer walk right; alternatively a price retention/escrow or deferred consideration tied to Bluefen revenue for 12 months post-completion.
- Ask whether the DD-006 privacy incident affects Bluefen data (see item 12) – that could affect Bluefen's willingness to consent.

**10. Riverlark Bank (DD-003) – AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-of-control 8.1; discharge 9.2.** "Release to be provided following Completion" is unacceptable on three grounds: (i) the deal is debt-free/cash-free, so this is a price deduction, not a post-completion formality; (ii) clause 8.1 almost certainly makes Completion an event of default, so for the period between Completion and release the Company is in default with security enforceable; (iii) the security probably extends to all assets and may include the shares themselves, which goes to title (item 16). Position: payoff letter from Riverlark before Completion; repayment at Completion out of the purchase price through the funds flow (directed payment); executed deed of release, PPSR discharge and any ASIC release delivered as completion deliverables in escrow, released simultaneously. Any shortfall or break costs are for the Seller's account.

**11. Completion bonuses (DD-005) – AUD 420,000.** "A matter for the Seller and not separately itemised" is the problem: unless the Seller actually pays them, the obligation sits in the Company and we will be funding them post-completion. Position: treat as a debt-like item / transaction cost deducted from the price in the funds flow, *grossed up* for employer on-costs (superannuation guarantee at 12%, NSW payroll tax at 5.45% and any leave accruals – budget roughly AUD 490–500k all-in), or have the Seller pay them directly at Completion with evidence. Also check the "continued-employment" conditions: if an employee leaves and the bonus lapses, that benefit should flow to whoever bore the cost, and we should confirm no retention arrangements survive that we are expected to fund separately.

**12. Ironquay Development Studio (DD-004, DD-010) – IP title conditional on payment; AUD 180,000 open.** Clause 7.3 means that until every SOW3 fee is paid in cleared funds, the Company does not own the SOW3 Project Materials. If those materials are part of the platform, we are paying AUD 24m for a business that does not own part of its product. An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" is inadequate because the loss, if Ironquay refuses to assign or asserts rights, is not AUD 180k – it is the value of the IP, re-development cost and potential infringement exposure. Position: (a) Seller to procure payment in full and a signed confirmatory assignment (with moral rights consents) *before* Completion as a CP or completion deliverable; (b) Seller to obtain written confirmation from Ironquay that no amounts are outstanding and no other SOWs have the same conditionality; (c) a specific indemnity covering all loss arising from any defect in title to any Ironquay-developed materials, outside the general cap; (d) ask for a bank-verified payment history, since the Seller itself says DD-010 is not independent verification.

**13. Export / privacy incident (DD-006).** The Seller characterises this as "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". It involves ~1,240 individuals' personal information sent to an unintended external recipient. Under the Privacy Act 1988 Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, the entity must complete an assessment within 30 days of becoming aware and notify the OAIC and affected individuals if there is likely serious harm. The investigation was "preliminary" on 22 September and we are now past 30 days – ask what has happened since. Also note the enhanced civil penalty regime and the statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy that now exist. Business contact details may or may not fall within the employee-records / business exemption depending on the content, and customer contracts (Bluefen in particular) very likely contain their own notification obligations, which may have been triggered irrespective of the statutory analysis. Position: completed investigation report before signing; specific warranty on the incident; specific indemnity (outside cap and basket) for all loss, regulatory action, customer claims and remediation cost; covenant to notify where required pre-completion with Buyer approval of communications; confirm whether any affected data subjects are outside Australia (GDPR / other regimes).

**14. Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011) – 3 × AUD 110,000.** The Disclosure Letter's own hedge ("does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course") undermines the Seller Update's "ordinary course" characterisation. Three identical amounts across two data-room documents suggests a single arrangement split into three – check whether that is to keep each below a materiality threshold in the warranties or a contract-approval limit. Position: obtain the underlying contracts; confirm whether the AUD 330k is committed, when it falls due and whether it is in the working-capital or debt-like adjustment; if it is a pre-completion commitment for post-completion benefit it should be reflected in the price mechanics; aggregate the three for all threshold purposes.

**15. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** Both disclosures are carefully worded to say what the clause does *not* say rather than what it does. Review the actual clauses ourselves. Lease: confirm whether the "notification obligation" is a pre-condition, whether failure gives the landlord termination or re-pricing rights, and build a pre-completion notice covenant. Mossvale: an assignment restriction may contain or be read with a change-of-control trigger; if there is any ambiguity, make it a CP or at least a Seller endeavours covenant with a specific indemnity.

**16. Title (DD-012).** The share register alone is not sufficient and the Seller expressly disclaims any Buyer verification. Before signing we should obtain: a current ASIC company extract and historical extract (to confirm share issues/transfers match the register), share certificates, a PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (to see whether Riverlark or anyone else has security over the shares), and confirmation of no options, convertible notes, employee equity or pre-emptive rights. Title warranties remain fundamental and uncapped (item 3).

---

## C. Summary of recommendations (in priority order)

1. **Do not accept the "FINAL" framing.** Confirm with Wattlebridge principals what, if anything, was actually agreed; respond on the basis that all non-headline terms are open.
2. **Fundamental / title / capacity / tax / IP-ownership warranties** carved out of the general regime: cap at 100% of price, survival for the statutory period (SPA as a deed), tax to at least 7 years.
3. **Delete clause 8.3 (buyer knowledge)** and replace general data-room/public-register disclosure with fair, specific disclosure against identified warranties; bring-down disclosure at signing and completion.
4. **Riverlark**: repay at Completion via funds flow with payoff letter and releases delivered simultaneously; never post-completion.
5. **Bluefen**: unconditional consent in Buyer-approved form plus satisfaction of 11.3 conditions as a CP; all-reasonable-endeavours covenant; walk right or retention if not obtained.
6. **Specific indemnities outside cap, basket and time limits** for: Ironquay IP title (not just the AUD 180k), the DD-006 privacy incident, pre-completion tax, and any Mossvale/lease consent failure.
7. **Funds flow**: deduct the AUD 420k bonuses grossed up for on-costs (~AUD 490–500k), and treat any committed Sandbar amounts appropriately in the debt/working-capital adjustment.
8. **General regime**: push cap to 30–50%; de minimis AUD 10k; tipping basket; aggregation of related claims; 24-month general survival; limitations apply only where expressly stated; carve out fraud, wilful default, specific indemnities, completion obligations and non-excludable statutory rights from clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5.
9. **Diligence before signing**: ASIC and PPSR searches; Ironquay payment/assignment status; completed privacy investigation and NDB assessment; actual text of the Bluefen 11.3 conditions, lease notification clause and Mossvale assignment clause; identity of DD-001.
10. **Consider W&I insurance** as a way to bridge the cap/survival gap, recognising that known matters (items 9–14) will be excluded and must be handled by price adjustment or specific indemnity.

This review is based solely on the documents provided and should be confirmed by Wattlebridge's external NSW counsel before positions are communicated to the Seller.
